NORTH CHICAGO, Ill. , Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV ) today announced the submission of a Biologics License Application (BLA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for etentamig, a second-generation BCMA x CD3 bispecific antibody T-cell engager administered intravenously for the treatment of adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. 1
BCMA-directed bispecific antibodies and CAR-T therapies have significantly changed the treatment landscape for people living with multiple myeloma. 2 However, their broader adoption may be limited by adverse events such as cytokine release syndrome, infections or neurotoxicity, as well as specialized administration and monitoring requirements. 2,3,4 Additionally, as disease relapses, treatment options in later lines of therapy become increasingly limited. Together, these factors highlight the need for additional therapies that may address the biology of the disease and help support effective treatment delivery across diverse care environments. 2,3,4
"Multiple myeloma is a chronic blood cancer that can reshape a person's life. Patients deserve therapeutic options that are not only effective, but also support the realities of when, where and how they receive treatment," said Daejin Abidoye, M.D., vice president and therapeutic area head, oncology, solid tumor and hematology, AbbVie. "This milestone brings us a step closer to potentially delivering a novel, patient-centered treatment option with a manageable safety profile and the convenience of a monthly dosing schedule that can help meet the needs of people living with multiple myeloma wherever they receive care."
The submission is supported by results from the global, Phase 3, multicenter, randomized CERVINO study evaluating etentamig versus investigator's choice of standard available therapies (SAT) in patients with triple-class exposed relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who had received at least two prior lines of therapy. 5 Topline results were announced earlier this year.
The findings indicated that etentamig achieved statistically significant improvements across the dual primary endpoints of overall response rate (74.0% vs. 45.7%) and progression-free survival (60% risk reduction) versus SAT. 5
The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) reported in the etentamig arm of the study (â¥ 25%) included cytokine release syndrome (CRS), hypogammaglobulinemia, neutropenia and anemia. 5 Discontinuations related to TEAEs were low for etentamig vs. SAT (3.6% vs. 14%). 5

With monthly dosing from initiation, etentamig demonstrated a potentially differentiated safety profile. 5 Among patients receiving a single step-up dose, the incidence of CRS was low (28.3%), all being grade 1 (23.9%) or grade 2 (4.4%) and no grade 3 or higher events were reported. 5 One patient experienced an immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) event (grade 1). Among all etentamig patients, grade 3/4 infections occurred in 27.7% versus 19.2% in patients receiving SAT. 5 Importantly, grade 5 infections were observed less frequently in patients treated with etentamig (1.5%) versus SAT (3.1%).

Multiple myeloma is a chronic blood cancer that affects white blood cells, called plasma cells, in the bone marrow. 6 It causes these cells to grow and crowd out healthy cells that help fight infection. 6 In 2025, an estimated 36,000 people were diagnosed with multiple myeloma in the U.S. 7 The disease commonly presents with non-specific symptoms that may resemble other conditions, leading to delays in diagnosis and treatment. 8 People living with multiple myeloma and their caregivers often face substantial physical, emotional and economic burden. 9
The Phase 3 CERVINO trial ( NCT06158841 ) is a global, multicenter, randomized, open-label study evaluating etentamig versus investigator's choice of standard available therapies (SAT) in triple-class exposed patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) who have received at least two prior lines of therapy, including exposure to a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory drug and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody. A total of 393 patients were randomized 1:1 to receive etentamig or SAT, including carfilzomib plus dexamethasone, elotuzumab plus pomalidomide and dexamethasone, or selinexor plus bortezomib and dexamethasone. Etentamig was administered using an optimized dosing strategy that incorporates a single step-up dose followed by monthly (Q4W) dosing from initiation. The dual primary endpoints are overall response rate and progression-free survival. Key secondary endpoints include overall survival, depth of response, measurable residual disease (MRD) negativity, disease symptoms and physical functioning.
Etentamig (ABBV-383) is an investigational, second-generation BCMA x CD3 bispecific antibody T-cell engager designed to combine meaningful anti-myeloma activity with a differentiated treatment experience for patients. Etentamig is composed of a low-affinity CD3 binding domain, designed to reduce cytokine release syndrome and infections, a high-affinity bivalent BCMA-binding domain, and retained FcRn binding enabling Q4W dosing after a single step-up dose. The direct connection between these structural findings and clinical effects is currently being investigated. 10
BCMA is highly expressed on the surface of malignant plasma cells in multiple myeloma, making it a key target for therapy. BCMA plays a crucial role in the survival of myeloma cells by promoting their growth and inhibiting their apoptosis (programmed cell death). 11
Several clinical studies are evaluating the potential of etentamig across diverse patient populations and treatment settings. To learn more about AbbVie's ongoing etentamig clinical trials, please visit clinicaltrials.gov.
AbbVie is committed to elevating standards of care and bringing transformative therapies to patients worldwide living with difficult-to-treat cancers. We are advancing a dynamic pipeline of investigational therapies across a range of cancer types in both blood cancers and solid tumors. We are focusing on creating targeted medicines that either impede the reproduction of cancer cells or enable their elimination. We achieve this through various, targeted treatment modalities and biology interventions, including small molecule therapeutics, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), immuno-oncology-based therapeutics, multispecific antibodies and novel CAR-T platforms. Our dedicated and experienced team joins forces with innovative partners to accelerate the delivery of potential breakthrough medicines.
Today, our expansive oncology portfolio comprises approved and investigational treatments for a wide range of blood cancers and solid tumors.
